Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, im Maya from Redwood, im the AE on the account. Sergio and I will run through the hosted API chat flow and answer questions.
[00:08] Elena: thanks, Maya. quick context — we're building an in-app assistant for enterprise customers. main goals: sub-500ms median latency for short queries, and cost ~<$0.001 per query if possible.
[00:18] Maya: great, yeah that's helpful. Sergio, i can hand over to you for the live demo?
[00:21] Sergio: yep, thanks. hi all. i'll share my screen in a sec — pulling up the Redwood Console and a small node/python SDK example. remember this is the hosted runtime so no infra on your side unless you later move to Dedicated or Private.
[00:36] Tom: quick Q — what counts as tokens? does sending whole history blow up cost?
[00:42] Sergio: good Q. tokens are measured client-side and billed per-token returned + input. history contributes, but we have prefix caching and you can set max_history or use the streaming partials to reduce bandwidth. also Console shows token breakdown per request under Metrics -> Token usage.
[01:05] Elena: can you demo streaming? we want users to see partial replies as they type.
[01:10] Sergio: sure — switching to SDK. code snippet: client.chat.create({model: 'redwood-1-chat', stream: true, messages: [...] , temperature: 0.2, max_tokens: 150}) and then attach an event listener for data chunks. when streaming=true the server yields deltas, you get lower time-to-first-byte and can show progressive output.
[01:28] Elena: that example — is the stream a websocket or SSE?
[01:32] Sergio: it's SSE over http/2 by default for the hosted api; the SDK abstracts it, and we also support http streaming for custom integrations. note: some corporate proxies may buffer SSE; if that's an issue you can use chunked responses or web socket proxy.
[01:52] Tom: what about retries? we saw 429s in earlier POC with another vendor and it blew up the app.
[01:58] Sergio: yep. recommended pattern: exponential backoff with jitter; on 429 do 500ms -> 1s -> 2s up to 4 attempts. for idempotency use request_id and set 'max_retries' in SDK. Redwood will also return a Retry-After header for rate-limit windows. we also have a server-side retry policy on the edge for transient 5xx.
[02:24] Priya: security — do you have SOC2 and how do you handle encryption?
[02:28] Maya: we are SOC2 Type II compliant, and we have enterprise packages that integrate with your KMS/HSM. for Private we can do customer-managed keys behind a VPC. i'll share the artifacts after the call.
[02:39] Priya: okay, also need SSO details — SAML/SCIM?
[02:43] Maya: yes SAML + SCIM for provisioning, RBAC in Console, audit logs for token usage.
[02:50] Elena: talk to us about params — temperature / top_p / max_tokens and sample tradeoffs.
[02:55] Sergio: temperature controls randomness — 0 is deterministic-ish; 0.7 is creative. top_p is nucleus sampling — you can use either. max_tokens caps the generated length. For moderation and safety you can set safety hooks and a stop sequence to prevent extra text. practical tip: start with temp 0.2-0.4 for assistant UIs. Also use presence_penalty / frequency_penalty on some models.
[03:28] Tom: we will need to throttle to keep under cost targets — any tools?
[03:32] Maya: Console has route-level quotas and per-token alerts. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization and predict cost improvements. For short chats batching is less useful but caching prefixes helps a lot.
[03:46] Elena: can console replay requests so we can debug latency spikes?
[03:50] Sergio: yes — tracing shows per-request token latency, kernel selection traces for larger seqs, and you can re-run a request with the exact prompt from Console Logs.
[04:03] Elena: ok demo time — show us streaming in real UI.
[04:07] Sergio: sharing a quick demo app — typed: "Summarize our refund policy in 3 bullet points." — you see the stream come in partial tokens at [04:10] first chunk, [04:12] second chunk. Time-to-first-byte about 80ms in this demo environment, backend average ~120ms for this model.
[04:28] Tom (interrupting): environment? is this in us-west or eu?
[04:31] Sergio: demo cluster in us-west. hosted API supports region routing, you can pin region in Dashboard or request geo-routing.
[04:40] Elena: are there any sticky pitfalls when integrating streaming? we saw doubled messages before.
[04:44] Sergio: common issues are client-side concatenation bugs and network retries replaying partial streams. best practice: event dedupe by sequence id, track chunk offsets; server supplies chunk ids. also set idempotency keys for retries so you don't double-count billing.
[05:06] Elena: billing question — do you bill partial streamed tokens?
[05:09] Maya: yes everything that's sent or generated counts — streaming is just a delivery mechanism. so token optimization matters.
[05:15] Tom: what's the SLA for hosted?
[05:18] Maya: hosted has SLOs but enterprise SLA is in Dedicated contracts. hosted has 99.5% regional availability historically, and we publish latency percentiles in the Console.
[05:29] Priya: for compliance we might need an on-prem option for pilot customers — is Private available?
[05:33] Maya: yes Private (VPC/on-prem) is an offering — it's more of an enterprise engagement and we can scope network/firewall rules. we'll pair Infra and SE on that next call.
[05:44] Elena: what about model variants and cost controls — can you automatically fallback to a cheaper model when under heavy load?
[05:51] Sergio: yes, policy routing. you can set fallback chains in the Deployment config: primary model redwood-1-chat, fallback to redwood-1-mini or a quantized variant. Console shows per-route overrides and you can set cost thresholds.
[06:10] Tom: are there per-customer rate limits? we need to ensure one tenant cant DOS others.
[06:14] Maya: yes per-API-key quotas, per-route quotas, and per-tenant isolation in Dedicated.
[06:20] Elena: show me the SDK snippet for retries and streaming together.
[06:23] Sergio: example in node: const stream = await client.chat.create({model:'redwood-1-chat', stream:true, temperature:0.3, max_tokens:120, request_id: 'bs-prompt-123'}); stream.on('data',(chunk)=>{/*dedupe by chunk.id*/}); stream.on('error', async err=>{ if(err.status===429){ await backoff(); retryWithSameRequestId(); } });
[06:53] Elena: the request_id — does that avoid double billing?
[06:56] Sergio: it prevents duplicate generation server-side for retries when idempotency is supported, but partial network retries that re-open a stream could still re-send bytes — we account for that. request_id greatly reduces duplicate compute.
[07:12] Tom: we have questions about latency breakdown — where are the big wins?
[07:15] Sergio: sequence length, model size, and kernel selection. for short prompts, model size dominates. Optimize can suggest smaller/quantized models with minimal quality loss. prefix caching reduces hot-path costs dramatically for conversational assistants.
[07:35] Elena: can you do canary rollouts? we need to test new model verisons with 5% traffic.
[07:39] Maya: yes Console supports canary A/B with traffic split and automated rollback on regression. we hook evals to monitor quality on your test prompts.
[07:50] Priya: audit logs — can we see who accessed what prompt?
[07:53] Maya: yes, Console audit logs show API key, request_id, time, and high-level token counts; full prompt content retention is configurable for compliance. for stricter needs we can disable retention entirely.
[08:07] Elena: show cost example for 1k daily chats of avg 80 tokens in/40 tokens out.
[08:11] Maya: quick calc — 1k * 120 tokens = 120k tokens/day ~ 3.6M tokens/month. at hosted list pricing that maps to X dollars — i'll send exact pricing tiers; Optimize can estimate savings from batch/caching.
[08:30] Tom: any known quirks with proxies and corporate networking?
[08:33] Sergio: some proxies buffer SSE as i mentioned; timeouts on long polling can drop connections — use keepalive pings and reconnect logic. also some corp proxies rewrite headers which can break chunked transfer encoding, so we recommend using our SDK which handles those cases.
[08:55] Elena: security follow-up: can we rotate keys programmatically and audit key usage?
[08:59] Maya: yes, API keys can be rotated via Console or APIs; we also support scoped keys, short-lived keys, and you can integrate your KMS.
[09:10] Sergio: demo finish — opened Console -> API -> Live Logs and clicked a request. you can see tokens, latency, model variant, kernel selection, and a small graph of per-token generation time.
[09:28] Elena: great. question: can we run a benchmark with our exact prompt set?
[09:31] Maya: yes. Next step: send us a sanitized prompt set (Priya approved) and we'll run a 48-hour benchmark on hosted and report latency/tokens and estimate cost.
[09:42] Tom: curious about cold start — does first request pay penalty?
[09:46] Sergio: model cold starts are minimal for hosted with warm pools; worst-case first request can be slightly slower if kernel JIT or memory warm-up occurs — but warm pools and your Dedicated option avoid that.
[09:58] Elena: we have concerns about hallucination safety — any tooling?
[10:01] Sergio: Redwood offers safety filters, post-processing rerankers, and we can integrate a deterministic tool-calling pattern to constrain outputs (structured JSON outputs with schema enforcement). Optimize also recommends prompt templates to reduce hallucinations.
[10:20] Priya: legal/procurement question — what's the contract length for Dedicated?
[10:24] Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits — typical enterprise deals are annual. terms vary; we'll run procurement thread after we finalize pilot numbers.
[10:36] Elena: any gotchas with retrofitting our existing chat UI?
[10:38] Sergio: main ones are: streaming integration, dedupe/state management, and token trimming for long histories. we can share code samples for React + SDK.
[10:50] Maya: ok let's recap next steps — we'll send pricing, SOC2 + ISO docs, SDK streaming example, and schedule the Dedicated/Private feasibility meeting.
[11:00] Elena: sounds good. thanks Maya & Sergio.
[11:03] Tom: thanks all.
[11:05] End of call.
